findings.message: The FAQ says data lives in your region "with retention rules and legal holds per record type". Retention is set per record type, but legal holds are not. A hold names a person or a matter (`privacy.legal_hold`, `packages/core/src/privacy/holds.ts`, `complete.ts:25`). Any rule with no `subject` column pauses entirely while any hold is active (docs/architecture.md, Retention and erasure). So the page tells buyers about a hold model the product doesn't have. The same sentence is in the 064 mock section (.specclaw/mock/index.html:2401). Fix both copies, for example: "with retention rules per record type and legal holds per person or matter".
findings.scenario: A buyer reads the FAQ and expects to place a hold on one record type, such as invoices. In the product a hold can only name a person or a matter, so they can't, and the copy doesn't match the product.

findings.message: The mock's hero queue sits under the selected PM tab, yet its first card is Liam's own "Add 2.5 h … Accept" draft. When it is pressed, the outcome line says "Accepted by Liam Walsh", so the PM's click is credited to Liam. That contradicts the page's own claim that every decision is attributed. The app's PM queue (queues.ts) has no such card, and the Engineer card says "Accepted by you, Liam Walsh · … · in chat". Fix: make the mock's PM queue match `QUEUES.PM`, or move this card under Engineer with the app's outcome text.
findings.scenario: In the mock, with the PM tab selected, press Accept → "✓ Accepted by Liam Walsh" appears, though the viewer (Chloe, the PM) made the decision.

findings.message:
The capability bands section has no heading of its own. Its `

` pitches come straight after the board's `

Today at Lumen Labs (fictional)

`, so the heading outline files "Delivery that updates itself." and the other bands under the board section. Fix: give `#product` a heading, which can be visually hidden (`

What amax covers

`), and update SECTIONS in marketing.spec.ts to match.
findings.scenario: A screen reader user lists headings → the five band headings appear as subsections of "Today at Lumen Labs (fictional)".

findings.message: Step titles default to muted (`.step b{color:var(--mut)}`). They only get full ink through the `on` class, which `HowStage`'s client effect adds. Server-rendered HTML, and any render where hydration fails or hasn't happened yet, shows all three titles as inactive. Make full ink the default and dim only when JS has marked a step inactive, e.g. `.how[data-live] .step:not(.on) b`.
findings.scenario: First paint before hydration, or JS blocked → every 'How it works' title is drawn in the muted colour, as if nothing is active.

findings.message: The video has `tabIndex={0}` before it starts, while `controls` is still false. That makes it a tab stop that does nothing: without controls, Space and Enter don't play it. Keyboard users land on it next to the Play button. Use `tabIndex={started ? 0 : -1}` so the video only takes focus once the native controls are there.
findings.scenario: Before pressing Play, Tab into the tour → focus lands on the bare video → Space does nothing.

findings.message: Pressing a queue card's action button unmounts that button (`{!done[c.id] && <button…>}`), so the focused element disappears and focus falls back to the document. Keep keyboard focus in place after the decision: move it to the card's `.ok` line (tabIndex -1) or to the next card's button.
findings.scenario: A keyboard user presses Enter on 'Approve week' → the button is removed → focus goes to <body>, and screen readers lose their place.

findings.message: The marketing captions now exist twice: `apps/web/public/marketing/amax-product.en.vtt` and `.specclaw/mock/media/amax-product.en.vtt`, which the mock plays. The same goes for the mp4 and poster. `marketing-prose.ts` only reads the apps/web copy, so the mock's captions can drift from it (for example, keep an old name or a 'logs time' line) without anything noticing. Either copy the mock media from the single apps/web source at build time, or add the mock's .vtt to `surfaces()`.
findings.scenario: The captions are edited in apps/web only → the mock keeps playing the old captions → no test notices the difference.
